(:577) with relative_to() containment checks raising Bad7zFile (:577-579 path=None branch against os.getcwd(), :583-586 path branch), Windows '\\\\?' long-path prefixing when outfilename.is_absolute() and not a UNC path (:596-597), targets filter f.filename not in targets (:598) - THE dominant attacker-controlled file-location input of this project; matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO source or sink row is expected to resolve at API level: the file-access channels flow through pathlib instance attributes on local variables (file/outfilename/fileish/path/target/src) and library-internal values (f.filename attribute reads, dict stores, argparse Namespace fields) that API graphs cannot bind to stdlib members, and pathlib/os/_winapi are not part of the database (only the py7zr tree is). The column is kept 'ast' for all families for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, f/args/pathlib/os name conventions). Member-name matching (.open/.stat/.joinpath/...) is receiver-name-agnostic on purpose: receiver identity cannot be proven syntactically (a .open() on a non-path object would be a name-collision row - the MemIO/NullIO duck-typed stubs in helpers.py:307-383 define .open/.mkdir/.parent but contain no call sites, so no stub rows are produced; receiver hints like fileish/outfilename/f.origin are emitted for the labeling step).

uncoveredCases: Dynamic dispatch / duck-typed IO stubs: Worker.register_filelike stores pathlib.Path or MemIO values into the target_filepath dict and every downstream member call (.parent/.mkdir/.open/.unlink/.touch) is resolved dynamically at runtime; the extraction matches member names receiver-agnostically, so a non-path object with the same member name would be a name-collision row (the MemIO/NullIO stub classes in helpers.py:307-383 define .open/.mkdir/.parent/.write/.read but contain no matching call sites, so no false rows are produced from their bodies).

Archive's own filename (operator input, not attacker-controlled): self.filename reads (py7zr.py:342/:356/:507/:934), cli.py:305 a.filename, cli.py:227/:284 archive_info.filename, and the fallback entry-name generation os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(self.filename)) at py7zr.py:513 are NOT emitted as source rows; only the __init__ file parameter row and the cli args.arcfile rows carry this input family.
Non-path CLI fields are not emitted: args.version (:97), args.verbose (:201/:323), args.password (:327/:404), args.volume (:392 via getattr) - none of them reaches a filesystem path.

Environment reads: the only os.environ/getenv read in the database is os.getenv('GITHUB_TOKEN') at utils/github_comment_bench.py:26 (a token, not a path); get_memory_limit()/blocksize come from py7zr/properties.py defaults, not env - no path-relevant env source exists, so no env family is emitted.

pathlib `/` operator constructions: none observed in the package (paths are built via pathlib.Path(...) and .joinpath(...)); if any existed they could not be distinguished from numeric division syntactically and would be documented here rather than extracted.

Pure path predicates with no filesystem access are not emitted: outfilename.is_absolute() (py7zr.py:596), is_windows_unc_path's path.drive.startswith('\\\\') (win32compat.py:213), .as_posix() conversions (py7zr.py:606/:830/:912/:1421/:1427/:1430), str(...) coercions (py7zr.py:659/:729/:1338). They are recorded here as guard/normalization evidence instead.

Entry-name backslash-to-slash normalization (the .replace('\\', '/') call at archiveinfo.py:757) IS emitted as a path_wrapper row because it rewrites separator semantics of the attacker-controlled name before it reaches the path pipeline.

multivolumefile.MultiVolume (external dependency, not in the database): its internal file open/stat operations are invisible; the visible boundary is the SevenZipFile.__init__ isinstance branch (py7zr.py:368-372) and the CLI constructions cli.py:205-207/:423.
